subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A bone marrow biopsy from a patient with suspected monoclonal gammopathy shows cells with an eccentric nucleus, clumped 'clock-face' chromatin, abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum, and a well-developed Golgi apparatus.
question: Which cell type is shown, and what is its principal function?

options.text: B lymphocyte, which presents antigen to helper T cells
Plasma cell, which produces large amounts of antigen-specific antibody
Plasmacytoid dendritic cell, which secretes interferon-alpha

explanation_correct: Plasma cells are terminally differentiated antibody-secreting cells with clock-face chromatin, an eccentric nucleus, abundant rough ER, and a prominent Golgi apparatus. They are found in bone marrow and normal peripheral lymphoid tissue and do not circulate in peripheral blood. Multiple myeloma is a plasma cell dyscrasia.

explanation_incorrect.A: B lymphocytes can present antigen and express CD20 but lack the abundant rough ER and clock-face chromatin of antibody-secreting plasma cells.
explanation_incorrect.C: Macrophages are phagocytes with kidney-shaped nuclei and tissue-specific names; they do not secrete large quantities of antibody.
explanation_incorrect.D: Megakaryocytes are large multinucleated cells that generate platelets and have nothing to do with immunoglobulin production.
explanation_incorrect.E: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells produce type I interferon and are not the antibody-producing cells described.

educationalObjective: Plasma cells have clock-face chromatin and abundant rough ER and secrete large amounts of antibody.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 68-year-old man has back pain and anemia. Serum protein electrophoresis shows a monoclonal spike, and skeletal imaging reveals punched-out lytic lesions. A bone marrow biopsy shows more than 10% clonal plasma cells.
question: Which disorder is best supported by these findings?

options.text: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance, because the M spike is <3 g/dL
Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, because IgM causes hyperviscosity
Multiple myeloma, a plasma cell dyscrasia with CRAB findings
Metastatic prostate carcinoma, because it produces blastic bone lesions
Chronic lymphocytic leukemia, because smudge cells are characteristic

explanation_correct: Multiple myeloma is a proliferation of a single plasma cell clone with monoclonal immunoglobulin production and CRAB features: hyperCalcemia, Renal insufficiency, Anemia, and Bone lytic lesions. Marrow biopsy shows more than 10% monoclonal plasma cells, typically with clock-face chromatin and intracytoplasmic immunoglobulin inclusions.

explanation_incorrect.A: MGUS has an M spike below 3 g/dL, fewer than 10% marrow plasma cells, and no CRAB end-organ findings; lytic lesions exclude it.
explanation_incorrect.B: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia produces IgM with hyperviscosity symptoms and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates, not punched-out lytic lesions.
explanation_incorrect.D: Prostate cancer metastases are blastic (sclerotic), not lytic, and would not produce a monoclonal plasma cell proliferation.
explanation_incorrect.E: CLL is a CD5+ B-cell neoplasm with smudge cells, not a plasma cell disorder with lytic bone destruction.

educationalObjective: Multiple myeloma is defined by clonal plasma cells and CRAB: hypercalcemia, renal failure, anemia, and lytic bone lesions.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A student examines a peripheral blood smear from a healthy adult and looks for plasma cells while reviewing the cellular elements of blood.
question: Which statement about plasma cells is correct?

options.text: They are the most abundant circulating leukocyte and have multilobed nuclei
They normally circulate in large numbers in peripheral blood
They are found primarily in bone marrow and normally do not circulate in peripheral blood
They are the immediate precursors of neutrophils in the marrow
They express CD3 and mediate cellular immunity

explanation_correct: Plasma cells are terminally differentiated B cells that reside in bone marrow and peripheral lymphoid tissues and normally do not circulate in peripheral blood. Their presence in blood is abnormal and suggests a plasma cell dyscrasia.

explanation_incorrect.A: Neutrophils are the most abundant circulating leukocytes and have multilobed nuclei; plasma cells are not numerous in blood.
explanation_incorrect.B: Circulating plasma cells are not a normal finding; they are tissue-resident antibody factories.
explanation_incorrect.D: Neutrophils arise from myeloid progenitors through myeloblasts and promyelocytes, not from plasma cells.
explanation_incorrect.E: CD3 is a T-cell marker; plasma cells are B-lineage cells and do not mediate cellular immunity.

educationalObjective: Plasma cells reside in marrow and lymphoid tissue and are not normally found in peripheral blood.
